📌 Do Miracles and Spiritual Gifts Prove Greater Spirituality?

Many Christians today think that the greatest thing God can do for you in this life is to let you experience a miracle, a vision, or a prophetic word. ✨ But friend, that’s not true.

👉 In popular teaching, “Holy Ghost power” (spiritual gifts) is often seen as the highest spiritual experience. And when churches don’t manifest those gifts, the usual excuse is:

“We don’t see them because the church is lukewarm.”

“If we had more faith, more fire, and more passion, God would send the miracles.”

“We don’t see it in the Philippines, but we do overseas where people have stronger faith.”

Sounds convincing, right? 🔥 But the Bible paints a very different picture.

📖 The Corinthians Had Spiritual Gifts… and Major Problems!

The church at Corinth was overflowing with signs, wonders, and spiritual gifts (1 Corinthians 12 lists more than anywhere else). Yet Paul describes them as:

• Carnal and immature (1 Cor. 3:1–3)

• Divided and proud (1 Cor. 1:10–13; 4:18)

• Tolerating sin (1 Cor. 5:1–2)

• Ignorant about doctrine (1 Cor. 15:12–34)

• Lacking in love (1 Cor. 13:1–3)

⚠️ If spiritual gifts were proof of deeper faith, stronger holiness, or greater maturity—then why did the most carnal church Paul wrote to display them more than anyone else?

Clearly, gifts were never meant to be the “pinnacle” of Christian experience.

📖 So Why Were They Given?

The answer comes when we see God’s progressive revelation. After Pentecost, the Spirit was poured out with signs and wonders (Acts 2:4, Heb. 2:4). But later, the risen Christ revealed to Paul a new program—the dispensation of the grace of God and the fellowship of the mystery (Eph. 3:1–9).

The Corinthians lived in a transition time:

• They had spiritual gifts 🕊️

• But they didn’t yet have the completed revelation of Christ through Paul 📜

This explains why gifts existed even among immature believers. They were temporary provisions until God’s “more excellent way” was revealed (1 Cor. 12:31; 13:8–10).

✨ The More Excellent Way Today

Today, we are not living in the Pentecostal program with miraculous signs. We are living in the dispensation of grace, where the emphasis is not on temporary signs, but on:

• The completed Word of God (2 Tim. 3:16–17)

• The sealing of the Spirit until the day of redemption (Eph. 1:13–14)

• Walking by faith, not by sight (2 Cor. 5:7)

• The power of Christ’s cross and grace working in us (Rom. 1:16; 2 Cor. 12:9)

💡 Miracles, tongues, and prophecies were never the highest revelation. They were a means to an end. The end is Christ revealed fully through the mystery committed to Paul.

🙏 Friend, don’t chase signs and wonders as if they prove maturity. The greatest thing God has done for you this side of heaven is not to give you a miracle—it’s to place you into Christ by grace through faith, seal you with His Spirit, and give you all spiritual blessings in heavenly places (Eph. 1:3).

That’s far greater than any temporary gift! 💖

💬 What do you think? Do you believe the church today is still under the program of signs and wonders, or under Paul’s gospel of grace?

📬 Follow for more teachings on Right Division, Mid-Acts Pauline Dispensationalism, and the simplicity that is in Christ.

Use these hashtags when sharing 👇
#RightDivision #MidActs #GospelOfGrace #PaulOurApostle #WalkByFaith
